title: Improving Native-Image Startup Performance
problem: Serverless/FaaS workloads have short lifetimes where startup time directly impacts service-level agreements. Despite AOT heap pre-initialization in GraalVM Native Image, startup remains suboptimal due to excessive page faults from poor binary layout.
motivation: Cloud runtime initiates programs upon request; startup overhead directly impacts SLA. Reducing page faults is critical for FaaS performance where startup dominates execution time.
method: Profile-guided binary reordering reorders code and objects in heap snapshots to minimize page faults. Proposes execution-order profiling to capture method and object access sequences. Three object ordering strategies reduce heap-related page faults. Matches profiled objects to built objects despite identity/persistence changes across Native Image builds.
key_novelty: First profile-guided approach to reorder heap snapshot objects in AOT-compiled Native Image binaries to reduce page faults.
contributions: Execution-order profiling for Native Image code and heap objects
Three object ordering strategies for heap snapshot optimization
Object matching technique across Native Image builds
1.61× average page fault reduction, 1.59× execution speedup
limitations: Evaluation limited to startup phase; impact on longer-running workloads not discussed.
primary_theme: Profile-guided startup optimization via binary reordering
